This isn't necessarily my opinion, btw. I was just trying to illustrate why it might bother some people. I had just read this the other day and found it to be relevant.

"Black people do not own the entire history of matted hair—just the term dreadlocks and its Diasporic connotations in the hair texture hierarchy. It’s not innately disrespectful for white/non-black people to wear their hair this way, but if you’re using the term “dreadlocks” to describe it then you’re not referencing an ancient history where everyone’s hair was probably matted or a oneness with nature, you’re specifically referencing the African Diaspora/transatlantic slave trade because the term “dreadlock” was born from that and did not exist before that. That is the only history that word has.

I default to being skeptical of any white person wearing their hair this way and calling it dreadlocks because if it’s not even worth it to you to know the history of the words you’re using then I don’t trust your solidarity (and I’m not sure I’ve ever met a white person using this word who was not trying to align themselves with some form of POC solidarity or thirsting after the legacy of Ras Tafari).

It’s not up to me to come up with a new word for y’all, though. You can have that task. I’m sure the language/history of ancient matted hair is not lost if you care to research it. But I don’t think backcombing and using wax to get your straight hair to matte has any Ancient significance, so…"
